review_scope: Civil: selected Cap. 12 provisions in the official consolidation through 2023. Criminal: Cap. 9 Articles 650–656, cited to the official consolidated text on legislation.mt; Article 650 was compared with it on 14 November 2026, Articles 651–656 are summarised from the statutory text hosted by UNODC through 2019. Report practice is corroborated by the e-Justice factsheet updated 22 June 2026. This is not a complete current-code audit.

expert_term.en: court expert; referee in civil procedure

appointment.basis: Code of Organization and Civil Procedure (Cap. 12), arts. 644–646
appointment.summary_en: The court orders a reference on a party's request or its own initiative and defines its object and directions.

questions.summary_en: Follow the object and directions set in the court's appointment decree.

items_en: Annex the parties' documents and witness depositions.
Plans or models require the court's direction or the parties' consent.

appointment.summary_en: The court appoints experts and records and serves its appointment decision.

questions.summary_en: The parties and court, and jurors where applicable, may seek clarification.

items_en: Facts and circumstances supporting the conclusions.
Oral or written report as directed; an oral report is reduced to writing.
Identify persons supplying factual information during the examination.

rights_duties.summary_en: Expert challenges and the oath are procedural steps; a generated archive does not perform them.

timestamp.qualified_recognition: Qualified timestamps carry date/time accuracy and data-integrity presumptions; qualification requires the statutory conditions.

open_questions: Trace amendments after the cited statutory editions before case-specific use. Articles 651–656 of the current Criminal Code were not compared with the 2019 text used for their summaries.

The e-Justice factsheet is official-hosted EEEI guidance, not the statute: https://e-justice.europa.eu/topics/find-legal-professional/find-expert/mt_en. The direct statutory texts are cited for the report fields.
The exact oath or declaration text, court-specific filing format and signer qualification require separate verification; none is invented here.
Report requirements are summarised in English. Native expert/law terms do not imply a complete reviewed translation of the report or interface.
court_language_notes: Maltese is the default court language. English use depends on the Judicial Proceedings (Use of English Language) Act and the court's directions; an English filing is not automatically accepted.
